summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for IdP configuration (Okta); source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] Placeholder values provided in the configuration are not intended for production use and must be replaced in a later step. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-auth-okta.md

[low] The Organization Owner role should be heavily restricted and not assigned to a human because it can change organization-wide settings and delete configurations. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/auth/authorization.md
[low] If the domain mapping is not created, SAML login will crash with an okta/hooks/acserror. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/mongodb-atlas-okta-integration-login-error/230897

[medium] While a federated IdP is enabled in Atlas, the platform disables any other authentication mechanisms. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-authentication.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/manage-federated-auth.md
[low] Atlas routes users with email addresses using mapped domains to the associated Identity Provider (IdP). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/federated-authentication.md

[low] Attribute names in the SAML configuration are case-sensitive and must be typed in camelCase as shown in the documentation. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/manage-federated-auth.md

[low] Once an IdP is linked to Atlas, it appears as Inactive in the Federation Management Console until at least one domain is mapped to it. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/manage-federated-auth.md

[low] Using the federation resource requires an existing identity provider (IdP) linked to the Atlas organization. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/operator/current/atlasfederatedauth-custom-resource.md
[low] For the Okta MongoDB integration, the Request Binding must be set to HTTP POST. Sources: https://saml-doc.okta.com/SAML_Docs/How-to-Configure-SAML-2.0-for-MongoDB-Cloud.html
[low] For the Okta MongoDB integration, the Response Signature Algorithm must be set to SHA-256. Sources: https://saml-doc.okta.com/SAML_Docs/How-to-Configure-SAML-2.0-for-MongoDB-Cloud.html
[low] For the Okta MongoDB integration, the Application username format must be set to Email. Sources: https://saml-doc.okta.com/SAML_Docs/How-to-Configure-SAML-2.0-for-MongoDB-Cloud.html

[low] The Okta MongoDB integration supports SAML-based Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM-based automated user provisioning to centralize account lifecycle management and govern role entitlements. Sources: https://www.okta.com/integrations/mongodb-atlas/
